text: {"headline":"High 99215 share concentrated on low-complexity patients is consistent with upcoding, but documentation is too thin to confirm or refute it.","leaning":"pattern_consistent_with_upcoding","interpretation":"The billing pattern, not the records, drives this leaning. 99215 rates run well above all-provider rates in every complexity band, including patients with zero or one chronic condition. Nearly half of the 99215s fall in that low-complexity group, and the sampled low-complexity 99215s carry simple diagnoses such as low back pain (C0054853, C0054967), rash (C0055022, C0055048) and follow-up-only codes (C0054987, C0055093, C0055197), which would rarely support high-complexity decision making. The records review cannot settle the question: only two 99215 claims were documented, and both supported the billed level (C0055106, C0055166). The 99214 below-billed rate is elevated relative to peers (C0054846, C0055017 documented as low MDM), and two notes claiming moderate-or-higher data review had no lab or test line, which is weak evidence of inflated notes. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims listed above, then compare the documented MDM and time against the billed level."}
